Pairwise Connectivity Among Focal Nodes From Random Dipoles

Source: R/dp-pairwise.R
dp_pairwise.Rd

Usage

dp_pairwise(
  resistance,
  locations,
  method = c("random", "exact"),
  resistance_is = "resistances",
  normalize = TRUE,
  n_draws = 32,
  seed = NULL,
  power = FALSE,
  progress = TRUE
)

Arguments

resistance

A terra::SpatRaster or file path: the resistance (or conductance) surface. Or a circuit from dp_circuit(), to reuse its factorization.

locations

The focal nodes: a two-column matrix or data frame of x and y coordinates (each snapped to the cell it falls in), or a terra::SpatRaster or file path on the same grid as resistance with a positive integer ID at each focal node's cell and 0 or NA elsewhere. Each node is one cell; focal regions of several cells aren't supported.

method

Character. "random" (default) for random dipoles, or "exact" for the exact sum from one solve per node.

resistance_is

Character. Whether resistance holds "resistances" (default) or "conductances". Ignored for a circuit.

normalize

Logical. Also compute flow potential (the same pairs on the uniform circuit, conductance 1 on the same cells) and normalized current. Default TRUE.

n_draws

Integer. Number of draws (solves) for method = "random". Default 32.

seed

Integer or NULL. Seed for the random draws. If NULL (default), one is drawn from R's random number generator, so set.seed() also makes runs reproducible. The seed used is returned as the "seed" attribute.

power

Logical. Also map the power dissipated (see "Power" in dp_omni()), and with normalize, normalized power. Default FALSE.

progress

Logical. Report progress through the 'progressr' package (see "Progress" in dp_omni()). Default TRUE; it shows only when a 'progressr' handler is active.

Value

A terra::SpatRaster with layers current; with normalize, flow_potential and normalized_current; with power, power; and with both, normalized_power, as in dp_omni(). With method = "exact", power sums to the pairs' total effective resistance, the power each pair's unit current dissipates. Attributes: "n_pairs", the number of pairs counted; for method = "random", also "halves" (see dp_omni()) and "seed".

Details

Maps connectivity among every pair of a set of focal nodes, the squared-current analogue of cs_pairwise()'s cumulative current map, at a cost that doesn't grow with the number of nodes.

Current flows along the circuit's links: the resistors joining each cell to its 8 neighbours (see dp_circuit()). For each link \(e\), the target is \(\sum_{i<j} I_e(i,j)^2\), over unordered pairs of focal nodes, where \(I_e(i,j)\) is the current through \(e\) when one unit flows from node \(i\) to node \(j\). A cell's value is \(\sqrt{\frac{1}{2}\sum_{e \ni \mathrm{cell}} (\cdot)}\) over its links, as in dp_omni(). Pairs are counted only within groups of cells connected to each other (no current passes across NA cells).

With method = "random", each draw injects \(\sum_{i<j} \xi_{ij}(e_i - e_j)\), every pair weighted by an independent standard normal \(\xi_{ij}\), and solves the circuit once; the mean squared current over draws estimates the target without bias. Its time hardly depends on the number of nodes (building each injection takes \(O(N^2)\), which is small next to a solve until \(N\) is in the thousands). With method = "exact", one solve per node gives the exact target, using \(\sum_{i<j}(y_i - y_j)^2 = N\sum_i y_i^2 - (\sum_i y_i)^2\) for each link, with \(y_i\) its current when node \(i\) is the source.

Current enters and leaves the circuit at the focal nodes, as in Circuitscape, but cell values count only the current on links. Circuitscape's cell maps also add the current injected or withdrawn at a cell before halving, so that a focal node's value includes the full unit it sends or receives; here, the current arriving from outside the circuit isn't counted, so focal nodes' cells read lower than in cs_pairwise(). Other cells, where current both enters and leaves along links, are unaffected.

Flow potential is the same quantity on the uniform circuit (with the same draws, for method = "random"), and normalized current is current divided by it, as in dp_omni(). Normalizing takes a second factorization and, for method = "exact", a second set of solves.

Reproducibility is as for dp_omni().

See also

cs_pairwise(), dp_omni(), dp_circuit()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # circuitscaper::cs_julia_available(circuitscape = FALSE)
resistance <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata/resistance.tif",
                                      package = "circuitscaper"))
set.seed(1)
nodes <- terra::spatSample(resistance, 30, xy = TRUE)[, 1:2]
result <- dp_pairwise(resistance, nodes, seed = 1)
exact <- dp_pairwise(resistance, nodes, method = "exact")
terra::plot(c(result$normalized_current, exact$normalized_current))
DONTSHOW({JuliaConnectoR::stopJulia()})
}
